s: Hello and welcome to Word Kitchen!
Today we are talking about work and career, a big part of everyday life.
Let us start with the most important person at work, your boss.
Your boss is the person in charge.
My boss is kind and fair.
A good boss listens and helps the team.
A bad boss only gives orders.
I think a kind boss makes the whole office happy.
Now, the people you work with are your colleagues.
I eat lunch with my colleagues every day.
One of my colleagues taught me a new skill last week.
Let us talk about money now, your salary.
A salary is the money you get every month for your job.
Lena, does a good salary make you happy at work?
But a high salary is not everything.
My friend has a big salary but works too much.
Before you get the job, you have the interview.
An interview is a meeting where people ask you questions for a job.
I have a job interview tomorrow.
A job interview can be stressful.
In the interview, they ask about your skills.
Then at work you have meetings.
A meeting is a time when people come together to talk about work.
The meeting starts at ten o'clock.
We have a meeting every Monday morning.
Our team meeting today was only twenty minutes.
At your desk, a table where you work.
My desk is near the window.
I keep my desk clean and tidy.
My desk is in the corner.
Every morning I clean my desk and start the computer.
A messy desk makes me nervous, so I like a tidy desk.
Sometimes work takes longer, and that is overtime.
Overtime is work you do after your normal hours.
My boss asked for overtime this Friday too.
But overtime also means more pay.
Now some good news, a promotion.
A promotion is a better job with more pay.
He got a promotion this year.
Lena, do you want a promotion?
I work hard for a promotion.
A promotion means new skills and a higher salary.
My dream is a promotion to team leader.
A customer is a person who buys things or services.
Always be kind to the customer.
If a customer has a problem, help fast.
Good customer service makes the company strong.
A deadline is the last day or time to finish something.
Our team finished before the deadline.
A clear deadline helps me plan.
Let us meet the deadline and celebrate after!
You know, Lena, I remember my first job.
My boss was strict, but my colleagues were so kind.
They helped me learn everything at my new desk.
My first job was hard too.
I had a small salary and lots of overtime.
But every meeting taught me something new.
A first job is always a lesson.
One day my boss called me to his office.
Was it about a promotion, or about a missed deadline?
He said the customer loved my work, and I got a promotion.
My salary grew, and I was so happy.
Hard work brings a promotion, a better salary, and happy customers.
Every interview, every meeting, every deadline is a step forward.
Let us quickly review: boss, colleague, salary, interview, meeting, desk, overtime, promotion, customer, deadline.
Use them every day and your English will grow.
See you next time on Word Kitchen!
